4962-the-story-of-germ-life.title: The Story Of Germ Life
4962-the-story-of-germ-life.creator: Unknown
4962-the-story-of-germ-life.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. he scale of plant and animal life. The middle chapters describe the functions of bacteria in the arts, in the dairy, and in agriculture. The final chapters discuss the relation of bacteria to disease and the methods by which the new and growing science of preventive medicine combats and counteracts their dangerous powers.

arxiv-2011-10782.title: Critical behavior of weakly disordered Ising model: Six-loop ε \sqrt{\varepsilon} expansion study
arxiv-2011-10782.creator: M. V. Kompaniets, A. Kudlis, A. I. Sokolov
arxiv-2011-10782.description: Abstract The critical behavior of three-dimensional weakly diluted quenched Ising model is examined on the base of six-loop renormalization group expansions obtained within the minimal subtraction scheme in 4 − ϵ 4-\epsilon space dimensions. For this purpose the ϕ 4 \phi^{4} field theory with cubic symmetry was analyzed in the replica limit n → 0 n\rightarrow 0 .

arxiv-2201-10084.title: Revisiting ℓ 1 \ell_{1} Loss in Super-Resolution: A Probabilistic View and Beyond
arxiv-2201-10084.creator: Xiangyu He, Jian Cheng
arxiv-2201-10084.description: Abstract Super-resolution as an ill-posed problem has many high-resolution candidates for a low-resolution input. However, the popular ℓ 1 \ell_{1} loss used to best fit the given high-resolution image fails to consider this fundamental property of non-uniqueness in image restoration.

arxiv-2203-16307.title: Information spreading and scrambling in disorder-free multiple-spin interacting models
arxiv-2203-16307.creator: Yoshihito Kuno 1, Takahiro Orito 2, Ikuo Ichinose 3
arxiv-2203-16307.description: Abstract Tripartite mutual information (TMI) is an efficient observable to quantify the ability of scrambler for unitary time-evolution operator with quenched many-body Hamiltonian. In this paper, we give numerical demonstrations of the TMI in disorder-free (translational invariant) spin models with 3-body and 4-body multiple-spin interactions.

arxiv-2205-04012.title: Improving negation detection with negation-focused pre-training
arxiv-2205-04012.creator: Hung Thinh Truong Timothy Baldwin Trevor Cohn Karin Verspoor
arxiv-2205-04012.description: Abstract Negation is a common linguistic feature that is crucial in many language understanding tasks, yet it remains a hard problem due to diversity in its expression in different types of text. Recent work has shown that state-of-the-art NLP models underperform on samples containing negation in various tasks, and that negation detection models do not transfer well across domains.

arxiv-2207-02650.title: Cooperative Beamforming for RIS-Aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO Networks Thanks: X. Ma and Z. Chen are with the National Key Laboratory of Science and Technology on Communications, University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Chengdu, China (e-mails: xymarger@126.com, chenzhi@uestc.edu.cn)
arxiv-2207-02650.creator: Xinying Ma, Deyou Zhang, Ming Xiao
arxiv-2207-02650.description: Abstract The combination of cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) and reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is envisioned as a promising paradigm to improve network capacity and enhance coverage capability. However, to reap full benefits of RIS-aided CF-mMIMO, the main challenge is to efficiently design cooperative beamforming (CBF) at base stations (BSs), RISs, and users.

arxiv-2210-08098.title: Liouville Theory and the Weil–Petersson Geometry of Moduli Space arXiv: 2210.08098
arxiv-2210-08098.creator: Sarah M. Harrison, Alexander Maloney, and Tokiro Numasawa
arxiv-2210-08098.description: Abstract Liouville theory describes the dynamics of surfaces with constant negative curvature and can be used to study the Weil-Petersson geometry of the moduli space of Riemann surfaces. This leads to an efficient algorithm to compute the Weil–Petersson metric to arbitrary accuracy using Zamolodchikov’s recursion relation for conformal blocks.

arxiv-2303-10043.title: Optimal liquidation with temporary and permanent price impact, an application to cryptocurrencies
arxiv-2303-10043.creator: Hugo E. Ramirez, Julián Fernando Sánchez López
arxiv-2303-10043.description: Abstract This paper studies the optimal liquidation of stocks in the presence of temporary and permanent price impacts, and we focus in the case of cryptocurrencies. We start by presenting analytical solutions to the problem with linear temporary impact, and linear and quadratic permanent impact.

arxiv-2304-01873.title: A Hamiltonian ratchet for matter wave transport
arxiv-2304-01873.creator: N. Dupont, L. Gabardos, F. Arrouas, N. Ombredane, J. Billy, B. Peaudecerf, D. Guéry-Odelin
arxiv-2304-01873.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by N. Dupont, L. Gabardos, F. Arrouas, N. Ombredane, J. Billy, B. Peaudecerf, D. Guéry-Odelin. We report on the design of a Hamiltonian ratchet exploiting periodically at rest integrable trajectories in the phase space of a modulated periodic potential, leading to the linear non-diffusive transport of particles. Using Bose-Einstein condensates in a modulated one-dimensional optical lattice, we make the first observations of this spatial ratchet, which provides way to coherently transport matter waves with possible applications in quantum technologies.

arxiv-2310-15633.title: Longitudinal kinematic imbalances in neutrino and antineutrino interactions for improved measurements of neutrino energy and the axial vector form factor
arxiv-2310-15633.creator: N. Baudis, S. Dolan, D. Sgalaberna, S. Bolognesi, L. Munteanu, T. Dieminger
arxiv-2310-15633.description: Abstract Current and future accelerator neutrino oscillation experiments require an improved understanding of nuclear effects in neutrino-nucleus interactions. One important systematic uncertainty is introduced by the collective impact of nuclear effects which bias the reconstruction of the neutrino energy, such as the nuclear removal energy.

arxiv-2312-03423.title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo Multi-Scan Data Association for Sets of Trajectories
arxiv-2312-03423.creator: Yuxuan Xia, Ángel F. García-Fernández, Lennart Svensson
arxiv-2312-03423.description: Abstract This paper considers a batch solution to the multi-object tracking problem based on sets of trajectories. Specifically, we present two offline implementations of the trajectory Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (TPMBM) filter for batch data based on Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling of the data association hypotheses.

arxiv-2402-10478.title: CodaMal: Contrastive Domain Adaptation for Malaria Detection in Low-Cost Microscopes
arxiv-2402-10478.creator: Ishan Rajendrakumar Dave, Tristan de Blegiers, Chen Chen, Mubarak Shah
arxiv-2402-10478.description: Abstract Malaria is a major health issue worldwide, and its diagnosis requires scalable solutions that can work effectively with low-cost microscopes (LCM). Deep learning-based methods have shown success in computer-aided diagnosis from microscopic images. However, these methods need annotated images that show cells affected by malaria parasites and their life stages.

arxiv-2411-10261.title: Partial Scene Text Retrieval
arxiv-2411-10261.creator: Hao Wang, Minghui Liao, Zhouyi Xie, Wenyu Liu, Xiang Bai
arxiv-2411-10261.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hao Wang, Minghui Liao, Zhouyi Xie, Wenyu Liu, Xiang Bai. The task of partial scene text retrieval involves localizing and searching for text instances that are the same or similar to a given query text from an image gallery. However, existing methods can only handle text-line instances, leaving the problem of searching for partial patches within these text-line instances unsolved due to a lack of patch annotations in the training data.

arxiv-2501-10472.title: Evaluating Gaussianity of heterogeneous fractional Brownian motion
arxiv-2501-10472.creator: Michał Balcerek, Adrian Pacheco-Pozo, Agnieszka Wyłomańska, Diego Krapf
arxiv-2501-10472.description: Abstract Heterogeneous diffusion processes are prevalent in various fields, including the motion of proteins in living cells, the migratory movement of birds and mammals, and finance. These processes are often characterized by time-varying dynamics, where interactions with the environment evolve, and the system undergoes fluctuations in diffusivity.

arxiv-2502-10093.title: Insights on the Scale of Leptogenesis from
arxiv-2502-10093.creator: Neutrino Masses
arxiv-2502-10093.description: Abstract We revisit the thermal leptogenesis scenario in the type-I seesaw framework featuring three heavy Majorana neutrinos with a hierarchical mass spectrum. We focus on low energy observables, specifically the lightest neutrino mass m ν lightest m_{\nu}^{\rm lightest} and the neutrinoless double-beta decay effective mass parameter m β ​ β eff m^{\rm eff}_{\beta\beta} .

arxiv-2507-08361.title: Access graph: a novel graph representation of public transport networks for accessibility analysis
arxiv-2507-08361.creator: Tina Šfiligoj*, Aljoša Peperko, Oded Cats
arxiv-2507-08361.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tina Šfiligoj*, Aljoša Peperko, Oded Cats. Abstract Accessibility, defined as travel impedance between spatially dispersed opportunities for activity, is one of the main determinants of public transport (PT) use. In-depth understanding of its properties is crucial for optimal public transport systems planning and design. Although the concept has been around for decades and there is a large body of literature on accessibility operationalisation and measurement, a unified approach is lacking.

arxiv-2508-04524.title: RAIDX: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation and GRPO Reinforcement Learning Framework for Explainable Deepfake Detection Conference: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia; October 27–31, 2025; Dublin, Ireland Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia
arxiv-2508-04524.creator: Tianxiao Li, Zhenglin Huang, Haiquan Wen, Yiwei He, Shuchang Lyu, Baoyuan Wu, Guangliang Cheng
arxiv-2508-04524.description: Abstract . The rapid advancement of AI-generation models has enabled the creation of hyperrealistic imagery, posing ethical risks through widespread misinformation. Current deepfake detection methods, categorized as face-specific detectors or general AI-generated detectors, lack transparency by framing detection as a classification task without explaining decisions.

arxiv-2509-20484.title: Data-Efficient Stream-Based Active Distillation For Scalable Edge Model Deployment
arxiv-2509-20484.creator: Dani Manjah*, Tim Bary*, Benoît Gérin, Benoît Macq and Christophe de Vleeschouwer
arxiv-2509-20484.description: Abstract Edge camera-based systems are continuously expanding, facing ever-evolving environments that require regular model updates. In practice, complex teacher models are run on a central server to annotate data, which is then used to train smaller models tailored to the edge devices with limited computational power.

arxiv-2602-00947.title: The Keyhole Effect: Why Chat Interfaces Fail at Data Analysis A Cognitive Science Framework for Hybrid Human-AI Interaction
arxiv-2602-00947.creator: Mohan Reddy

pmc-10618184.title: How being perceived to be an artist boosts feelings of attraction in others
pmc-10618184.creator: Eugen Wassiliwizky, Paul Wontorra, Fredrik Ullén
pmc-10618184.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Music production is a universal phenomenon reaching far back into our past. Given its ubiquity, evolution theorists have postulated adaptive functions for music, such as strengthening in-group cohesion, intimidating enemies, or promoting child bonding. Here, we focus on a longstanding Darwinian hypothesis, suggesting that music production evolved as a vehicle to display an individual’s biological fitness in courtship competition, thus rendering musicality a sexually selected trait. We also extend this idea to visual artists.

pmc-11198441.title: Racial and Ethnic Variation in ECMO Utilization and Outcomes in Pediatric Cardiac ICU Patients
pmc-11198441.creator: Marissa A Brunetti, Heather M Griffis, Michael L O'Byrne, Andrew C Glatz, Jing Huang, Kurt R Schumacher, David K Bailly, Yuliya Domnina, Javier J Lasa, Michael Alice Moga, Hayden Zaccagni, Janet M Simsic, J William Gaynor
pmc-11198441.description: BackgroundPrevious studies have reported racial disparities in extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) utilization in pediatric cardiac patients.ObjectivesThe objective of this study was to determine if there was racial/ethnic variation in ECMO utilization and, if so, whether mortality was mediated by differences in ECMO utilization.MethodsThis is a multicenter, retrospective cohort study of the Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium clinical registry.

pmc-11517185.title: 8.N. Scientific session: Transferability and adaptation of vaccination interventions: Learning from underserved communities
pmc-11517185.creator: Organised by: RIVER-EU, Chair persons: Tamara Schloemer (Netherlands), Janine De Zeeuw (Netherlands)
pmc-11517185.description: Removing barriers in the health system that make it difficult for cultural, religious or ethnic minorities to access vaccinations is an urgent concern in order to prevent infectious diseases in the future. Childhood vaccine uptake for MMR and HPV in most underserved communities is lower than in the general population.

pmc-11642344.title: Numerical, Physical, and Industrial Investigations on Hot Metal Desulphurization—From Macromixing Conditions to Reaction Rate Phenomena
pmc-11642344.creator: Adam Cwudziński, Jan Falkus, Angelika Podolska-Loska
pmc-11642344.description: The efficiency of the hot metal pretreatment process plays a very important role in achieving high-quality and low-cost advanced steel. From macromixing phenomena obtained by numerical modeling and physical experiments to compound interaction databases from industry trials, the Authors compared fundamental relationships from the literature with their own laboratory results and plant data.

pmc-11657885.title: Comparison of fine-scale malaria strata derived from population survey data collected using RDTs, microscopy and qPCR in South-Eastern Tanzania
pmc-11657885.creator: Issa H Mshani, Frank M Jackson, Elihaika G Minja, Said Abbasi, Nasoro S Lilolime, Faraja E Makala, Alfred B Lazaro, Idrisa S Mchola, Linda N Mukabana, Najat F Kahamba, Alex J Limwagu, Rukia M Njalambaha, Halfan S Ngowo, Donal Bisanzio, Francesco Baldini, Simon A Babayan, Fredros Okumu
pmc-11657885.description: BackgroundMalaria-endemic countries are increasingly adopting data-driven risk stratification, often at district or higher regional levels, to guide their intervention strategies. The data typically comes from population-level surveys collected by rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs), which unfortunately perform poorly in low transmission settings.

pmc-11691263.title: HOME HEALTH CARE ACCESS AND OUTCOMES AMONG VULNERABLE OLDER POPULATIONS: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES
pmc-11691263.creator: Emily Gadbois, Michael Johnson
pmc-11691263.description: Home health care (HHC) provides skilled nursing (e.g., wound care, medication management), therapies (e.g., physical, occupational, speech), and aide services (e.g. bathing, grooming, dressing), which are key supports necessary to regain function, restore health, and maintain independence in the community.

pmc-11862726.title: Prevalence and Risk Factors of Burnout Among Medical Residents in Tunisia: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11862726.creator: W. Haouari, S. Omri, A. Labyadh, I. Gassara, R. Feki, N. Charfi, J. Ben Thabet, M. B. Maalej, N. Smaoui, L. Zouari, M. Maalej
pmc-11862726.description: IntroductionThe burnout syndrome is a blend of physical exhaustion and emotional fatigue that impairs an individual’s performance at work. In Tunisia, factors like working hours, the frequency of monthly shifts, and the physical and emotional abuse that physicians face from patients have collectively led to a significant incidence of burnout among medical professionals.

pmc-12718220.title: Virtual Reality as a Window into Sibling Aggression
pmc-12718220.creator: Sheila R van Berkel, Andrea L Haccou, Catharina E Bergwerff
pmc-12718220.description: Sibling aggression is the most common form of domestic violence, which can have a negative impact on both child and adolescent mental health. The few previous studies that investigated aggression between siblings, assessed aggression primarily through self- or parent-report, with the limitation of reporter bias.

pmc-12848112.title: Clinical outcomes of intra-articular corticosteroid injection vs. multimodal physiotherapy in patients with frozen shoulder in short term: a randomized clinical trial
pmc-12848112.creator: Mohammad Ali Zare, Mohammad Hosein Ebrahimzadeh, Ali Moradi, Afsaneh Zeinalzadeh, Salman Nazary-Moghadam
pmc-12848112.description: This study aimed to compare the short-term effects of multimodal physiotherapy (MPT) with intra-articular corticosteroid injection (IAI) on pain, disability, effectiveness of treatment, and passive range of motion in patients with frozen shoulder. Randomized Controlled Trial. University Hospital. Patients diagnosed with frozen shoulder with at least 50% passive range of motion (PROM) limitation.

pmc-13057416.title: Clozapine for treatment‐resistant schizophrenia with epilepsy: A case report
pmc-13057416.creator: Toru Horinouchi, Mayusa Mito, Toshiyuki Ishikawa, Yuichi Nakamura, Shuhei Ishikawa, Naoki Hashimoto
pmc-13057416.description: BackgroundTreatment‐resistant schizophrenia (TRS) poses a substantial clinical challenge for which clozapine (CLOZ) is the only effective treatment. However, clinicians may hesitate to prescribe CLOZ for TRS patients with epilepsy due to its presence because CLOZ is contraindicated in patients with uncontrolled epilepsy in some countries including Japan.Case PresentationA 36‐year‐old male with TRS and focal epilepsy underwent CLOZ therapy.

pmc-13395608.title: Posaconazole mitigates α-amanitin-induced liver injury by inhibiting STT3B-mediated glycosylation and cellular uptake
pmc-13395608.creator: Bei Wang, Chenwei Wang, Yizhi Zhang, Yingjie Yu, Jiahao Yuan, Pan Chen, Jie Chen, Yubo Tang, Qiao-Ping Wang, Ke-Jing Tang
pmc-13395608.description: BackgroundMushroom poisoning caused by Amanita phalloides, primarily mediated by the toxin α-amanitin (AMA), frequently leads to fatal liver failure, yet no specific antidote is currently available. Although AMA is known to inhibit RNA polymerase II, its complete cytotoxic mechanism remains unclear.

pmc-13424054.title: Acoustic Flutter Processing in the Inferior Colliculus of Awake Marmosets: Complementary Rate Coding Modulated by Acoustic Parameters
pmc-13424054.creator: Siyi Bai, Xinyuan Cao, Min Xie, Guanglong Sun, Xiaohui Wang, Leilei Zheng, Xinjian Li, Zheng Lin, Lixia Gao
pmc-13424054.description: The acoustic flutter is processed through complementary monotonic rate coding and cannot be modulated by other acoustic parameters in the auditory cortex (AC). However, it remains unclear how the inferior colliculus (IC) encodes acoustic flutter, especially when changing other acoustic parameters.

pmc-13535802.title: Aortic valve repair for treatment of aortic regurgitation in patients with a bicuspid aortic valve: the experience of a single Polish aortic centre
pmc-13535802.creator: Jakub Jasinski, Ryszard Bachowski, Marek Jasiński, Radoslaw Gocol
pmc-13535802.description: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV)–related aortic regurgitation presents heterogeneous anatomic phenotypes that complicate durable valve repair. To ensure repair reproducibility, current guidelines recommend specialised aortic centres with transparent, published outcomes. This report summarizes the two-decade experience of a single Polish aortic centre integrating clinical, imaging, and surgical data to develop a standardized, phenotype-driven repair strategy.

pmc-13635256.title: Self-assembly of surface layer protein SbsC from Geobacillus stearothermophilus and common principles of Bacilli S-layers
pmc-13635256.creator: Christoph Grininger, Lavinia Gambelli, Anđela Đordić, Markus Eder, Christoph Buhlheller, Theo Sagmeister, Gustav Oberdorfer, Janet Vonck, Uwe B Sleytr, Walter Keller, Bertram Daum, Tea Pavkov-Keller
pmc-13635256.description: S-layers are (glyco)protein coats displayed on the external surface of many bacterial and archaeal species. By combining X-ray crystallography, electron cryo-tomography and SymProFold predictions, we propose the structure of the self-assembled S-layer protein (SLP) SbsC from the Gram-positive bacterium Geobacillus stearothermophilus ATCC 12980. SbsC consists of nine domains arranged like beads on a string.

pmc-13657847.title: Glaucocalyxin A sensitizes ovarian cancer cells to PARP inhibitors by inducing DNA damage
pmc-13657847.creator: Lingling Zhuang, Lanyan Hu, Qi Chen
pmc-13657847.description: BackgroundPoly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) have demonstrated therapeutic advantages in ovarian cancer (OC) patients with homologous recombination (HR) deficiency. However, their effectiveness is limited in HR-proficient or acquired resistance tumors. Glaucocalyxin A (GLA) is an ent-kauranoid diterpene with anti-tumor properties.
